# Risk Register

| ID    | Risk                                                                | Impact | Planned control                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | -----: | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| R-001 | False positives caused by dynamic JSX values                        |   High | Right-to-left effective-attribute resolution, exact/partial/dynamic confidence, unknown-case suppression, negative fixtures, and documented limits                                                                |
| R-002 | False negatives from component abstractions                         |   High | Intrinsic-only stable rules, source/component association scopes, preserved relationships/locations, and explicit custom-wrapper/icon/alias limitations                                                           |
| R-003 | Parser incompatibility with valid syntax                            |   High | Exact Babel 8 adapter, source-kind-specific plugins, four-language fixture matrix, typed per-file isolation with sibling continuation, and documented syntax limits                                               |
| R-004 | Symlink loops or traversal outside project                          |   High | Fail-closed default/invalid-policy link skipping; opt-in canonical containment, target exclusions, visited realpaths, and cycle/external-link tests                                                               |
| R-005 | Malicious source text injected into HTML report                     |   High | Hostile-Unicode neutralization then HTML escaping, fixed markup/CSS, no-script CSP, safe-URL revalidation, inert fallbacks, and structural XSS tests                                                              |
| R-006 | Large projects consume excessive memory/time                        | Medium | Exclusions, bounded source bytes/AST visits/static text/model depth, one sequential parse per candidate, deterministic inventory, and reproducible benchmarks                                                     |
| R-007 | Rule errors terminate the entire audit                              | Medium | Exact-once evaluation, transactional per-rule result validation, stable normalized execution errors, safe-sibling continuation, and isolation/determinism tests                                                   |
| R-008 | Agent changes architecture while solving a local task               |   High | Active ExecPlan, contracts, traceability, architecture gate                                                                                                                                                       |
| R-009 | Documentation and state drift                                       | Medium | State validator, exact base/final evidence contracts, source digest, two-run comparison, SHA-256 finalization, identity rechecks, non-destructive failed cleanup, documented rename residual, and closure updates |
| R-010 | Dependency or supply-chain vulnerability                            |   High | Exact lockfile, strict peers/scripts, immutable action SHAs, Dependabot, CodeQL, Dependency Review, and audit evidence                                                                                            |
| R-011 | UX rule claims exceed static-analysis capability                    |   High | Explicit intrinsic/literal/component scopes, advisory confidence and wording, configurable reviewed sets/thresholds, limitations, and evidence-based promotion                                                    |
| R-012 | GitHub push or PR automation unavailable                            |    Low | Local commits, explicit blocker record, no false success claims                                                                                                                                                   |
| R-013 | Current toolchain packages have incompatible engine or peer ranges  | Medium | Pin exact reviewed versions, enforce Node.js 24/npm engines and strict peers, preserve the lockfile, and verify the resolved tree                                                                                 |
| R-014 | CLI output exposes native details or injects terminal controls      | Medium | Shared per-value sanitizer covers controls, bidi, BOM, and lone surrogates; only fixed badges add ANSI; stable errors, injected streams, no native causes, and hostile-output tests                               |
| R-015 | Root permissions or canonical target change after preflight         | Medium | Reauthorize root and file identity/containment around a no-follow descriptor read, fail closed on observed changes, isolate local failures, and document residual TOCTOU                                          |
| R-016 | Hosted CI behavior differs from local verification                  | Medium | Three stable runner images, exact Node/action versions, portable smokes, workflow dispatch, and post-push status review                                                                                           |
| R-017 | Malformed configuration executes code or merges ambiguously         |   High | Bounded descriptor-only UTF-8 JSON loading with regular-file identity checks; closed versioned plain-data validation; explicit null/empty semantics; defaults < file < CLI; stable errors                         |
| R-018 | Report output escapes the root or overwrites unrelated data         |   High | Fixed names, segment/root identity checks, in-root link rejection, exclusive no-follow creation, bounded sync/close writes, final authorization, stable errors, and explicit TOCTOU limits                        |
| R-019 | Reporters disagree or mutate the normalized audit result            | Medium | One frozen result, exact JSON, complete terminal/HTML records, shared fixture, coordinate-aware cross-reporter tests, deterministic reruns, and input snapshots                                                   |
| R-020 | CLI integration misclassifies success or claims unwritten reports   |   High | Source-aware CLI overrides, preserved exit `0/2/3` boundaries, reserved `1`, direct trusted terminal output, writer-confirmed claims only, ordered multi-write failure tests, and no unsafe rollback              |
| R-021 | Controlled validation data drifts from executable rule behavior     |   High | Closed canonical manifest, exact physical/case/count tests, real built-CLI execution twice, reviewed expected maps, stable projection comparison, and no derived-from-actual expectation rewrite                  |
| R-022 | Controlled precision/recall is generalized beyond its small corpus  |   High | Per-rule results, explicit instance denominators, unsupported cases outside metrics, no inflated TN, retained identities/rationales, and repeated corpus-only limitation statements                               |
| R-023 | One-machine performance observations are presented as portable      | Medium | Five complete fresh-root runs over a versioned 240-file scale, individual/min/median/max durations, sampled child VmRSS method and limits, exact environment, and no machine-dependent pass threshold             |
| R-024 | Expert heuristic review is misrepresented as participant usability  |   High | Versioned expert method/tasks, scripted-time labels, participant count zero, testing unexecuted, SUS N/A/null, and no satisfaction or population claim                                                            |
| R-025 | Evidence leaks secrets, drifts, or overwrites a valid first package |   High | Credential-free allowlisted snapshot, source digest, exact artifact contract, sanitization, stable/volatile comparison, two-run preservation, SHA-256 manifest, and bounded finalizer                             |
| R-026 | Static module resolution links the wrong component                  |   High | Direct relative imports only; Babel binding identity; exact one-candidate resolution; unresolved ambiguity; normalized paths; positive, negative, shadowing, and platform tests                                   |
| R-027 | Component composition cycles or expansion consume unbounded work    |   High | Store links without expansion; cycle-aware traversal; bounded depth and visited-state checks; deterministic ordering; focused cyclic fixtures                                                                     |
| R-028 | The v0.2 experiment destabilizes the deliverable v0.1.0 baseline    |   High | Immutable baseline tags, isolated milestone branch, unchanged published package/demo, mandatory regression gate, no merge or publication on no-go                                                                 |
| R-029 | The six-hour spike consumes delivery time without proving viability |   High | Fixed deadline at 2026-07-31T15:38:04-06:00; exact gate scenarios; M07 closure report; abandon integration if linking, cycles, composition, or regressions remain red                                             |
